_doc: M6-A highlight scoring. Read by sim/highlights.gd AFTER a match finishes —
nothing here can change how a match plays out, only which parts of it are
worth watching. Tuning this is safe.
merge_window_s / merge_radius: two things this close in time AND space are
one moment. A gank, the tower it buys and the dragon that follows should
read as one thing, the way a viewer would see it.
score.*: the weights. kill/multikill/ace/participant/gold_per_1000 are per
unit; the kind names (dragon, baron, tower_*, nexus, and the fight sizes)
are flat bonuses added once per component of that kind. late_bonus scales
the whole score by game clock: 0.6 means a moment at the last minute is
worth 1.6x the same moment at minute zero.
The tower_* keys follow the tiers in data/map.json, which is the only place
that decides how many towers a lane has. tower_inner is kept but currently
dead: the middle tier was removed on 2026-08-09. An unlisted kind scores 0,
so adding a tier back to map.json only needs a weight here if you want the
reel to notice it.
select.*: the reel. floor is absolute — a boring match gets a SHORT reel,
it never gets padded. min_spacing_s stops five clips of one long brawl.
max_per_kind is variety. The nexus is exempt from all of it.
director.*: M6-C, read by game/main.gd (not sim/highlights.gd — these are new
top-level keys the loader just passes through). preroll_s/aftermath_s pad each
moment's [start, end] into the window the camera treats as "inside this
highlight" — REPORTS/M6-scoping.md measured fights at 6.3s mean/8s p90, so a
few seconds either side comfortably covers the approach and the comedown
without reaching into the next moment. zoom is the camera's close-up zoom
level while a highlight is active (same 1.0-4.0 range as MapView.ZOOM_MIN/MAX).
rewind_s is the transport rewind button's step. Precise minute-budget tuning
against the designer's ~11-12 / ~4-5 min targets is M6-F, not this file.
